metadata.scenario: A nurse calls the office from a patient's home to report that she completed the morning visit and the patient's vitals are stable. She asks if there are any schedule changes for the afternoon. Quick staff coordination call.

transcription.text: CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I help you today? Hi, Margaret. This is William Chen. I just had a nurse visit this morning. Hi, William! How did the visit go? The nurse completed her assessment, and she said my vitals are stable. That’s great to hear! Any concerns you want to discuss? No major concerns, but I wanted to check if there are any schedule changes for this afternoon. Let me check on that for you. One moment, please. *[pause]* Okay, I see we have a Personal Care Assistant scheduled for 3 PM. Great! Is everything still on track for that? Yes, she is confirmed. I’ll notify the caregiver. Perfect! I really appreciate your help. Of course, William! While I have you, would you be interested in adding some Companion Care? What does that involve? It includes social interaction, light housekeeping, and even meal prep if needed. It’s $25 to $30 per hour. That sounds appealing. How many hours would you recommend? A couple of hours a few times a week could really help with your recovery. Okay, let’s consider it. I’ll think about it after the afternoon visit. Sounds good! I’ll follow up with you tomorrow to check in. That would be great. Thank you! You’re welcome, William. Just a quick note, I'll also send a reminder for your medications. Perfect! I sometimes forget them. No problem! We’ll set that up. Any other questions? Not right now. Thank you for your assistance! You’re very welcome! Have a great day, William. You too, Margaret! Bye. Bye!
